metadata.title: Articulated Structures Glossary Terms
notes: Alphabetic glossary entries were deduplicated by term slug.
When duplicate alphabetic entries existed, the most complete/longest entry was selected as primary and alternate entries were preserved under alternate_entries.
Core-framework definitions not present in the A-Z glossary were added so the JSON covers the whole glossary foundation.

terms.definition: A device that produces controlled movement, force, or rotation in a mechanical or structural system.
terms.engineering_relevance: Actuators are used in deployable roofs, movable bridges, robotic arms, adaptive facades, cranes, and kinetic structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can treat an actuator as a prescribed displacement, prescribed rotation, applied force, or controlled motion input.

terms.definition: A structure capable of changing shape, stiffness, position, or response according to loading, environment, or control input.
terms.engineering_relevance: Adaptive structures combine structural mechanics with sensing, actuation, and control.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can classify adaptive structures separately from passive articulated systems.

terms.definition: The maximum permitted displacement, rotation, sliding, uplift, or deformation under service or design conditions.
terms.engineering_relevance: Bearings, expansion joints, hinges, and sliding joints are designed with movement capacity limits.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compare calculated movement with allowable movement and generate warnings when limits are exceeded.

terms.definition: A bolt used to connect a structural member, base plate, bearing, or support assembly to concrete or foundation material.
terms.engineering_relevance: Anchor bolts may transfer tension, shear, moment, or combined loading depending on base connection behaviour.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include anchor bolts in connection detailing and support restraint checks.

terms.definition: The rotational movement of a body, member, or joint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Angular displacement is central to hinges, semi-rigid joints, bearings, rocking systems, and deployable mechanisms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should output angular displacement in radians or degrees.

terms.definition: A curved structural form that primarily transfers load through compression and horizontal thrust.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulated arches may be two-hinged, three-hinged, tied, fixed, or bearing-supported.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include arch templates with thrust, reaction, bending, and hinge-force outputs.

terms.definition: The main curved compression member of an arch.
terms.engineering_relevance: The arch rib carries axial compression, bending, and shear depending on shape, loading, and support conditions.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model the arch rib as a curved member or segmented frame approximation.

terms.definition: A beam with one or more hinges, releases, or bearing-supported segments that alter moment continuity.
terms.engineering_relevance: Gerber beams and suspended-span systems are common examples.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support internal hinge placement and automatically split bending moment diagrams at hinge points.

terms.definition: A frame containing pins, hinges, semi-rigid joints, or releases that modify the usual rigid-frame behaviour.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulated frames are used in portals, cranes, temporary works, roof structures, and mechanical support systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow mixed rigid and released joints in the same frame model.

terms.definition: A joint that permits selected relative movement while still transferring selected forces.
terms.engineering_relevance: The joint may rotate, slide, rock, or twist depending on its detailing.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should define articulated joints by their released and restrained degrees of freedom.

terms.definition: A structure made of members connected by joints, hinges, pins, bearings, sliders, links, or semi-rigid connections that allow controlled relative motion or controlled release of force/moment transfer.
terms.engineering_relevance: It appears in trusses, cranes, bridges, deployable roofs, robotic arms, foldable structures, three-hinged arches, movable frames, suspension systems, and bearing-supported bridge decks.
terms.app_solver_relevance: In the app, this is the parent system category. Every model must define members, nodes, joints, degrees of freedom, restraints, releases, loads, and stability checks.

terms.definition: The deliberate provision of movement or release at a connection, support, or internal point of a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulation reduces unwanted restraint forces, allows thermal movement, simplifies force flow, accommodates rotation, and can make a structure statically determinate.
terms.app_solver_relevance: In the app, articulation is recorded as a joint property: rotation release, sliding release, axial release, shear release, torsional release, or semi-rigid stiffness. CHAPTER 2. ARTICULATED STRUCTURES: CORE FRAMEWORK

terms.definition: Change in member length caused by axial tension or compression.
terms.engineering_relevance: Axial deformation can control truss displacement, cable extension, tie elongation, and strut shortening.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute axial deformation using member force and axial stiffness.

terms.definition: Internal force acting along the length of a member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Positive axial force is often treated as tension and negative axial force as compression, depending on sign convention.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should display axial force diagrams and member tension/compression classification.

terms.definition: A release that prevents axial force transfer across a member end, joint, or connection.
terms.engineering_relevance: Axial releases are less common than moment releases and must be used carefully because they can destabilize a model.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn users when axial releases create disconnected or unstable systems.

terms.definition: A joint that allows rotation about multiple axes while transferring force through a common center.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is the mechanical equivalent of a spherical joint and appears in spatial linkages and some bearing assemblies.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can model it as a joint with rotational freedoms and translational restraints.

terms.definition: A seismic protection strategy where the structure is supported on devices that reduce transmission of ground acceleration.
terms.engineering_relevance: Base isolators allow controlled lateral displacement while supporting vertical load.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model isolators as lateral springs, dampers, or nonlinear bearing elements.

terms.definition: A component placed between a superstructure and substructure to transfer load while permitting selected movement or rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Bearings are critical in bridges, industrial structures, equipment supports, and long-span roofs.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include bearing type, movement direction, rotation capacity, vertical load capacity, and lateral restraint.

terms.definition: A failure condition where a bearing loses its intended movement capacity due to corrosion, debris, damage, misalignment, or lock-up.
terms.engineering_relevance: Seized bearings can create unintended restraint forces and cracking in bridge decks or supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include bearing seizure as a reality-check warning in inspection mode.

terms.definition: Internal moment that causes curvature of a member.
terms.engineering_relevance: In articulated systems, moment may be intentionally released at hinges and pins.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should show zero moment at ideal hinges and reduced moment at semi-rigid joints.

terms.definition: A diagram showing how bending moment varies along the length of a member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moment diagrams reveal whether a structure is bending-dominant, axial-dominant, or release-controlled.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should generate BMD outputs for beams, frames, arches, and articulated members.

terms.definition: A mathematical statement of how a support, joint, or edge restrains movement or force.
terms.engineering_relevance: Boundary conditions determine reactions, displacements, stability, and internal force distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should translate user-selected supports into solver boundary conditions.

terms.definition: A member added to resist lateral movement or stabilize a frame, truss, or mechanism.
terms.engineering_relevance: Braces often carry axial tension or compression and prevent sway or collapse mechanisms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should identify whether braces stabilize the structure or are themselves compression-buckling risks.

terms.definition: A bearing used in bridges to transfer vertical loads and accommodate rotation, expansion, contraction, creep, shrinkage, and sometimes seismic movement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Bridge bearings may be fixed, guided, free-sliding, elastomeric, pot, spherical, or isolation bearings.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include a bridge-bearing module for load transfer, movement allowance, and warning checks.

terms.definition: Instability of a compression member or system under axial load or combined loading.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulated systems often rely on slender struts, ties, and braces; compression members require buckling checks.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag compression members and compute preliminary slenderness or Euler buckling warnings.

terms.definition: A flexible tension-only member that carries load through axial tension and cannot resist compression or bending in the ideal model.
terms.engineering_relevance: Cables appear in suspension bridges, stayed roofs, cranes, hangers, nets, and deployable structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat cables as tension-only elements and warn when compression appears.

terms.definition: The vertical deviation of a cable from a straight chord under self-weight or applied load.
terms.engineering_relevance: Sag affects cable tension, horizontal thrust, deflection, and geometry.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support sag estimation or catenary/parabolic approximation for cable systems.

terms.definition: The natural curve formed by a flexible cable under its own weight.
terms.engineering_relevance: The catenary is compression-arch logic reversed: a hanging cable in tension can define an efficient arch shape in compression.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can use catenary logic for cable and funicular-form explanation.

terms.definition: A forked connection with a pin passing through aligned holes, allowing rotation about the pin axis.
terms.engineering_relevance: Clevis connections are common in rods, ties, actuators, linkages, cranes, and mechanical supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify clevis connections as pin-type articulated joints.

terms.definition: A motion pattern that forms when a structure develops enough releases, hinges, or failures to lose stability.
terms.engineering_relevance: Collapse mechanisms can form through plastic hinges, support failure, member buckling, or accidental over-release.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should detect mechanism formation and distinguish it from safe controlled articulation.

terms.definition: The condition that connected structural parts must deform consistently without impossible separation or overlap.
terms.engineering_relevance: Compatibility is especially important in indeterminate and semi-rigid articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should enforce compatibility at rigid joints and controlled relative compatibility at articulated joints.

terms.definition: A member carrying axial compression.
terms.engineering_relevance: Compression members include struts, columns, arch ribs, braces under compression, and top chords of trusses.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag compression members for buckling, slenderness, and end-condition checks.

terms.definition: A support that resists compression but cannot resist tension.
terms.engineering_relevance: Soil contact, masonry seating, some bearings, and uplift-sensitive foundations behave as compression-only supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow support uplift and contact loss in nonlinear mode.

terms.definition: A numerical measure of how sensitive a matrix solution is to small errors or perturbations.
terms.engineering_relevance: A high condition number may indicate near-instability, poor scaling, weak restraints, or badly conditioned stiffness relationships.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use condition number as a solver health indicator.

terms.definition: The physical detailing that realizes a joint condition, such as bolting, welding, pinning, bearing seating, clevis connection, or gusset plate assembly.
terms.engineering_relevance: The assumed analytical joint and the real construction connection may differ. A connection assumed pinned may behave semi-rigid; a connection assumed fixed may slip or rotate.
terms.app_solver_relevance: In the app, connection type should be separate from ideal joint assumption so that reality-check warnings can be generated. 2.2 Articulation Logic Application in App / Solver For every articulated structure, the app should ask five primary questions: 1. Which degrees of freedom are free? 2. Which degrees of freedom are restrained? 3. Which internal force components are transferred? 4. Which internal force components are released? 5. Does the remaining system stay stable after releases are applied? 2.3 Degrees of Freedom

terms.definition: A condition that restricts a degree of freedom.
terms.engineering_relevance: A fixed support provides several constraints, while a roller support provides fewer. The number and arrangement of constraints determine stability.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should count constraints and warn when the system is under-constrained or over-constrained.

terms.definition: An equation that imposes a relationship between degrees of freedom.
terms.engineering_relevance: Constraint equations are used for rigid links, multi-point constraints, guided supports, symmetry, and kinematic mechanisms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use constraint equations for advanced articulated systems and mechanism modules.

terms.definition: Nonlinear behaviour caused by opening, closing, sliding, separation, impact, or changing contact surfaces.
terms.engineering_relevance: Examples include uplift supports, gap elements, rocking bases, sliding bearings, and compression-only contact.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat contact nonlinearity as an advanced analysis mode.

terms.definition: A joint introduced to control cracking, shrinkage, or movement in concrete, masonry, tile, or cladding systems.
terms.engineering_relevance: A control joint is not automatically a structural hinge, but it may affect force transfer and movement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish architectural/control joints from true structural articulation.

terms.definition: A projecting structural arm used to lift or move loads.
terms.engineering_relevance: Crane booms are often pin-connected, braced, lattice-like, and stability-sensitive.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include crane-boom templates with pin joints, axial members, load radius, and stability warnings.

terms.definition: An internal hinge located near the crown of an arch or the apex of a frame.
terms.engineering_relevance: A crown hinge makes a three-hinged arch statically determinate and reduces thermal or settlement-induced moment.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include crown hinge placement for three-hinged arch templates.

terms.definition: A device or modelling element that dissipates energy through velocity-dependent, frictional, hysteretic, or material-based resistance.
terms.engineering_relevance: Dampers are used in seismic isolation, vibration control, cable systems, movable bridges, tall structures, and adaptive articulated frames.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include dampers as optional dynamic or semi-dynamic elements connected to selected degrees of freedom.

terms.definition: Permanent load due to the self-weight of structural and non-structural components.
terms.engineering_relevance: Dead load is usually the baseline load for beams, frames, arches, trusses, bridges, roofs, and articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow automatic self-weight generation based on material density, cross-section, and member length.

terms.definition: The displacement of a member or structure under load.
terms.engineering_relevance: Deflection controls serviceability in beams, trusses, bridge decks, roofs, cranes, and articulated frames.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should output deflection diagrams, maximum deflection values, and serviceability warnings.

terms.definition: The displaced configuration of a structure after loads, support movements, or imposed actions are applied.
terms.engineering_relevance: The deformed shape helps identify sway, rotation, hinge action, mechanism tendency, uplift, and bearing movement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should plot exaggerated and true-scale deformed shapes.

terms.definition: An independent displacement or rotation needed to describe the movement of a joint, member, or body.
terms.engineering_relevance: In a 2D frame node, the usual degrees of freedom are horizontal displacement, vertical displacement, and in-plane rotation. In a 3D frame node, three translations and three rotations may be required.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The solver must build the global stiffness matrix using active degrees of freedom, restrained degrees of freedom, and released degrees of freedom.

terms.definition: The number of redundant force or displacement unknowns beyond what can be solved using independent equilibrium equations alone.
terms.engineering_relevance: Indeterminacy determines whether equilibrium-only analysis is enough or whether stiffness/compatibility methods are required.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute an approximate degree of indeterminacy and use it to guide solver selection.

terms.definition: A structure designed to fold, unfold, expand, retract, or change configuration through articulated joints and linkages.
terms.engineering_relevance: Deployable structures appear in temporary roofs, space structures, kinetic facades, shelters, cranes, scissor systems, and emergency structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat deployable structures as both kinematic systems and structural systems after deployment.

terms.definition: The condition describing whether all reactions and internal forces can be obtained from equilibrium equations alone.
terms.engineering_relevance: Determinate systems are usually easier to analyse but may have less redundancy. Indeterminate systems require compatibility and stiffness analysis.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify each structure as determinate, indeterminate, unstable, or mechanism-like.

terms.definition: Linear or angular movement of a point, joint, support, member, or body.
terms.engineering_relevance: Displacement may be caused by load, temperature, settlement, prestress, actuation, creep, shrinkage, or dynamic excitation.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should track translational and rotational displacements separately.

terms.definition: A structural analysis method in which unknown displacements and rotations are solved first, then internal forces are recovered.
terms.engineering_relevance: The matrix stiffness method is a major computational form of the displacement method.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use displacement-method logic for frames, beams, semi-rigid joints, spring supports, and complex articulated systems.

terms.definition: A load spread over a length, area, or volume instead of being applied at a single point.
terms.engineering_relevance: Distributed loads include self-weight, floor loads, wind pressure, snow load, hydrostatic load, and equipment loading.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support uniform, linearly varying, patch, trapezoidal, and user-defined distributed loads.

terms.definition: A bending condition where a member bends in opposite curvature over different portions of its length.
terms.engineering_relevance: Double curvature appears in sway frames, fixed-end members, partially restrained frames, and some articulated frame systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can identify double-curvature bending from the bending moment diagram.

terms.definition: Lateral displacement of a storey, frame, tower, pier, or structural system.
terms.engineering_relevance: Drift is important in frames, base-isolated structures, seismic systems, bridge piers, cranes, and tall articulated assemblies.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute total drift and inter-storey drift where relevant.

terms.definition: A load that varies with time and may produce inertial or vibration effects.
terms.engineering_relevance: Dynamic loads include earthquake, wind gusts, moving machinery, crane operation, vehicle motion, impact, and human-induced vibration.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can initially support dynamic loads as equivalent static loads, with future dynamic modules.

terms.definition: A connection in which the line of action of force does not pass through the centroidal axis or intended joint center.
terms.engineering_relevance: Eccentricity creates secondary bending moments, torsion, local stress, and unexpected joint demand.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag eccentric connections and optionally generate secondary moment checks.

terms.definition: The offset distance between a load path, member axis, connection center, or reaction line and the reference centroidal axis.
terms.engineering_relevance: Small eccentricities can produce significant secondary moments in articulated systems, especially at pins, bearings, brackets, and gusset plates.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow eccentricity input for realistic joint and connection modelling.

terms.definition: The equivalent buckling length of a compression member considering end restraints and joint behaviour.
terms.engineering_relevance: Pinned, fixed, semi-rigid, and sway conditions change the effective length of columns, struts, braces, and compression chords.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should estimate effective length factor based on end condition and warn when compression members are slender.

terms.definition: A support that restrains movement through finite stiffness instead of perfect fixity.
terms.engineering_relevance: Soil, elastomeric bearings, springs, flexible foundations, pads, and support plates often behave elastically rather than rigidly.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model elastic supports using translational and rotational spring constants.

terms.definition: A bearing made of rubber-like material, often laminated with steel plates, that supports vertical load while allowing rotation and shear deformation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Elastomeric bearings are common in bridges and building isolation systems because they accommodate movement and rotation.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include elastomeric bearing properties such as vertical stiffness, shear stiffness, rotation capacity, and movement limit.

terms.definition: A mathematical representation of a structural part used in analysis, such as a bar, beam, frame member, cable, spring, gap, or rigid link.
terms.engineering_relevance: Elements convert physical members into solvable equations.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should map user geometry into solver elements.

terms.definition: The stiffness matrix representing the force-displacement relationship of one structural element.
terms.engineering_relevance: Element stiffness matrices are assembled into the global stiffness matrix.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use element stiffness matrices internally while exposing user-friendly structural terms externally.

terms.definition: The restraint condition at a member end, such as fixed, pinned, free, guided, semi-rigid, or released.
terms.engineering_relevance: End conditions strongly affect bending moments, deflection, buckling length, and force distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should require explicit end conditions for each member.

terms.definition: A release applied at the end of a member to remove transfer of a selected force or moment component.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moment end releases are common in frame models to represent pin connections.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support end-release input and automatically update the stiffness formulation.

terms.definition: The conversion of mechanical energy into heat or other forms through damping, friction, yielding, hysteresis, or material deformation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Energy dissipation is essential in seismic systems, base isolation, dampers, sliding joints, and controlled rocking systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include energy dissipation as an advanced feature for dynamic and seismic modules.

terms.definition: The condition where total forces and total moments balance.
terms.engineering_relevance: Equilibrium is required for the whole structure, each member, each joint, and each free-body diagram.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include numerical equilibrium residual checks after solving.

terms.definition: The elastic instability of a slender compression member under axial load.
terms.engineering_relevance: Pinned, fixed, and semi-rigid end conditions change the critical buckling load.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include preliminary Euler buckling checks for struts, compression chords, braces, and columns. Formula / Relation Euler critical load for an ideal compression member: Pcr = π2EI (KL)2 where Pcr is the critical load, E is Young’s modulus, I is second moment of area, K is effective length factor, and L is actual member length.

terms.definition: A bearing that permits longitudinal or transverse movement due to temperature change, creep, shrinkage, settlement, or other imposed actions.
terms.engineering_relevance: Expansion bearings prevent thermal lock-in and unwanted restraint forces.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify bearings as fixed, guided, free, or expansion type.

terms.definition: A joint designed to permit relative movement between structural or non-structural parts.
terms.engineering_relevance: Expansion joints are common in bridges, long buildings, pavements, facades, roofs, and industrial structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish expansion joints from structural hinges because they may not carry the same internal forces.

terms.definition: A hinge located at a support or boundary of a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: External hinges allow rotation while restraining selected translations.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat hinged supports as reaction-generating supports with no ideal moment restraint.

terms.definition: Progressive damage caused by repeated cyclic loading.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulated structures with pins, bearings, cables, bolts, crane members, and bridge components may be fatigue-sensitive.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag cyclic-load cases and fatigue-prone details for inspection notes.

terms.definition: A crack that initiates and grows under repeated stress cycles.
terms.engineering_relevance: Fatigue cracking often occurs at stress concentrations, weld toes, bolt holes, pin holes, gusset plates, and bearing details.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include fatigue crack as a defect category in inspection and diagnostics mode.

terms.definition: A bearing that restrains horizontal movement while allowing rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Fixed bearings establish a reference point for bridge or deck movement and transfer lateral loads to substructure.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should identify fixed-bearing locations and route lateral forces accordingly.

terms.definition: A joint that prevents relative rotation and transfers bending moment, shear, axial force, and sometimes torsion.
terms.engineering_relevance: Fixed joints create moment continuity and make frames stiffer, but may attract secondary forces due to settlement or temperature.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat fixed joints as full compatibility connections unless semi-rigid behaviour is specified.

terms.definition: A support that restrains both translation and rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: In 2D, a fixed support provides horizontal reaction, vertical reaction, and moment reaction.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should generate all applicable reaction components for a fixed support.

terms.definition: The bending stiffness of a member, equal to EI.
terms.engineering_relevance: Higher flexural rigidity reduces curvature and deflection under bending.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use EI to compute beam, frame, and arch bending response.

terms.definition: A structure designed to fold through hinges, joints, flexible panels, or linkage mechanisms.
terms.engineering_relevance: Foldable structures are used in temporary shelters, deployable roofs, aerospace structures, kinetic installations, and portable construction systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include foldable structures in the deployable-mechanism category.

terms.definition: An analysis method where redundant forces are selected as unknowns and compatibility equations are used to solve them.
terms.engineering_relevance: The force method is useful for indeterminate beams, arches, frames, and support-settlement problems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can use force-method explanations for educational mode even if the backend uses stiffness analysis.

terms.definition: The process by which loads pass through a connection, joint, member, bearing, or support.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulated structures require careful definition of which forces are transferred and which moments are released.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should describe force transfer at every joint type.

terms.definition: A structural system whose members can carry axial force, shear force, and bending moment.
terms.engineering_relevance: Frames may be rigid-jointed, pinned, braced, semi-rigid, or articulated.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support frame templates with mixed joint conditions.

terms.definition: A structural body isolated from its surroundings for equilibrium analysis.
terms.engineering_relevance: Free-body analysis makes support reactions, hinge forces, member forces, and load paths visible.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should generate free-body views for members, joints, and whole systems.

terms.definition: A member end with no support restraint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Cantilever tips, overhangs, suspended spans, and projecting arms may contain free ends.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat free ends as unrestrained and warn if the whole structure becomes unstable.

terms.definition: A separated diagram of a member, joint, or whole structure showing all applied loads, reactions, internal forces, and moments.
terms.engineering_relevance: Free-body diagrams are the foundation of hand analysis for trusses, beams, arches, cranes, and articulated frames.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should generate free-body diagrams for selected members, supports, and joints.

terms.definition: Surface damage caused by small repeated relative motion between contacting parts.
terms.engineering_relevance: Fretting can occur at pins, bearings, bolted joints, sliding plates, and cable sockets.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include fretting as a defect mode in inspection and maintenance reports.

terms.definition: A connection where force transfer depends partly or fully on friction between contact surfaces.
terms.engineering_relevance: Friction joints may slip if the friction capacity is exceeded.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include friction limit checks in advanced connection mode.

terms.definition: A shape that carries a particular loading pattern mainly through axial force with minimal bending.
terms.engineering_relevance: Cables, arches, hanging chains, compression shells, and some articulated systems use funicular logic.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should explain whether a structure is bending-dominant or funicular/axial-dominant.

terms.definition: A modelling element that permits free movement until a specified gap closes, after which contact force develops.
terms.engineering_relevance: Gap elements are useful for bearings, uplift, impact stops, expansion joints, and contact supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include gap elements in nonlinear contact mode.

terms.definition: The condition that connected members fit together after deformation without impossible separation or overlap.
terms.engineering_relevance: Compatibility is essential for indeterminate structures, semi-rigid joints, frames, and systems with imposed settlement or temperature movement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should enforce compatibility according to joint type and release condition.

terms.definition: A condition where deformation changes the equilibrium equations or force path significantly.
terms.engineering_relevance: Large displacement, cable sag, arch thrust, P-∆ effects, snap-through, and rocking systems may require geometric nonlinear analysis.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should mark geometric nonlinearity as an advanced solver option.

terms.definition: A continuous beam system made statically determinate by inserting internal hinges.
terms.engineering_relevance: Gerber beams reduce bending continuity and allow simpler reaction calculation, but hinge placement controls moment distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include Gerber beam templates with internal hinge placement.

terms.definition: The reference coordinate system used for the entire structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Member forces and stiffness are often computed locally, then transformed into global coordinates.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should show node coordinates, support directions, and load directions in the global system.

terms.definition: Equilibrium of the complete structure under applied loads and support reactions.
terms.engineering_relevance: Global equilibrium checks verify that total horizontal forces, vertical forces, and moments balance.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report equilibrium residuals after solving.

terms.definition: The assembled stiffness matrix representing the complete structural model.
terms.engineering_relevance: It combines element stiffness, support restraints, joint releases, spring supports, and constraints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app uses this internally for matrix stiffness analysis.

terms.definition: A load acting due to gravity, usually vertically downward.
terms.engineering_relevance: Gravity loads include self-weight, floor loads, equipment loads, roof loads, and imposed occupancy loads.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support gravity-load generation for all structural systems.

terms.definition: A bearing that allows movement in one direction while restraining movement in another.
terms.engineering_relevance: Guided bearings are used in bridges and long-span systems to control expansion direction and lateral load path.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow guide direction input and generate lateral restraint reactions accordingly.

terms.definition: A support that allows translation along a selected direction while restraining translation perpendicular to that direction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Guided supports represent sliding blocks, rails, guide slots, and constrained bearing movement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should define guided supports using local guide-axis orientation.

terms.definition: A plate used to connect multiple members, commonly in trusses, bracing systems, cranes, towers, and steel frames.
terms.engineering_relevance: Gusset plates transfer axial, shear, and sometimes moment effects between members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include gusset plates as connection-detail components in report mode.

terms.definition: A tension member suspending a deck, beam, pipe, roof, or load from a cable, arch, truss, or supporting frame.
terms.engineering_relevance: Hangers are common in suspension bridges, tied arches, suspended roofs, industrial supports, and mechanical services.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model hangers as tension-dominant or tension-only members.

terms.definition: A joint or release that allows rotation while transferring selected force components.
terms.engineering_relevance: Hinges reduce or eliminate bending moment transfer and are central to articulated beams, arches, frames, trusses, and mechanisms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should represent hinges as rotational releases and show zero or reduced moment transfer.

terms.definition: The internal force transmitted through a hinge.
terms.engineering_relevance: Even when bending moment is zero at a hinge, axial and shear forces may still be transmitted.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report hinge force components separately from hinge moment.

terms.definition: An axis about which rotation occurs.
terms.engineering_relevance: Hinge-line orientation matters in slabs, shells, foldable panels, bridge bearings, and 3D articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support hinge-axis definition in 3D models.

terms.definition: A support that restrains translation but permits rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: In 2D, a hinged support usually provides horizontal and vertical reactions but no moment reaction.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should map hinged support to translational restraints and released rotation.

terms.definition: The horizontal reaction component generated by arches, cables, tied systems, frames, and inclined members.
terms.engineering_relevance: Horizontal thrust is critical for arch foundations, tied arches, suspension systems, and portal frames.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute and explain thrust paths.

terms.definition: A structural system combining multiple behaviours, such as frame action, truss action, cable action, arch action, bearing movement, or deployable mechanism behaviour.
terms.engineering_relevance: Many real structures are hybrid rather than purely pinned, fixed, or cable-based.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow mixed modelling components in a single model.

terms.definition: Energy-dissipating behaviour where the unloading path differs from the loading path.
terms.engineering_relevance: Hysteresis appears in dampers, yielding steel, friction devices, base isolators, rocking systems, and cyclic joint behaviour.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include hysteresis in future seismic and nonlinear modules.

terms.definition: A short-duration load applied suddenly due to collision, falling object, machinery action, vehicle impact, crane operation, or accidental contact.
terms.engineering_relevance: Impact can produce forces much larger than equivalent static loading because inertia and energy transfer become important.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can initially model impact as an equivalent static load with a warning that full dynamic analysis may be required.

terms.definition: A prescribed movement applied to a support, joint, member end, actuator, or bearing.
terms.engineering_relevance: Support settlement, thermal expansion, jack movement, actuator stroke, and foundation shift can all be modelled as imposed displacement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow imposed displacement inputs and compute resulting reactions and internal forces.

terms.definition: A prescribed angular movement applied at a joint, support, hinge, bearing, or actuator.
terms.engineering_relevance: Imposed rotation may occur in rocking systems, bearing seats, mechanical linkages, movable bridges, and controlled deployable structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support imposed rotation as a boundary or actuation input.

terms.definition: A diagram showing how a response quantity changes as a unit load moves across a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Influence lines are important for bridges, cranes, gantries, moving loads, and articulated beam systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include influence-line generation for reactions, shear, moment, and deflection at selected points.

terms.definition: A small deviation from perfect geometry, alignment, straightness, verticality, or connection position.
terms.engineering_relevance: Initial imperfections affect buckling, stability, second-order effects, crane booms, columns, struts, and slender articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include imperfection warnings for compression-dominant and stability-sensitive models.

terms.definition: The point about which a body or link appears to rotate at a particular instant.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is useful in mechanism analysis, linkages, deployable systems, and moving articulated frames.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can use instantaneous center logic in kinematic explanation mode.

terms.definition: A force developed within a member or connection as a result of external loads, restraints, and compatibility.
terms.engineering_relevance: Common internal forces include axial force, shear force, bending moment, and torsion.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should output internal forces member-wise and joint-wise.

terms.definition: A hinge located within a member span or inside the structural system rather than at an external support.
terms.engineering_relevance: Internal hinges release bending moment while usually transferring axial force and shear.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should split member continuity at internal hinge locations and force bending moment to zero at ideal hinges.

terms.definition: The ability of the member arrangement itself to remain geometrically stable after supports and releases are considered.
terms.engineering_relevance: A structure can have enough external reactions but still be internally unstable if members form a mechanism.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should check both external support stability and internal member-layout stability.

terms.definition: A joint that separates adjacent components to prevent unwanted force transfer, cracking, vibration transfer, or restraint interaction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Isolation joints are used in buildings, slabs, equipment foundations, cladding, pavements, and expansion zones.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish isolation joints from load-transferring structural hinges.

terms.definition: A numerical solution procedure that improves an approximate answer through repeated updates.
terms.engineering_relevance: Iterative solvers are useful in nonlinear contact, cable systems, large-displacement analysis, and semi-rigid connection calibration.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can use iterative solvers for advanced nonlinear modules.

terms.definition: A device used to apply force, displacement, lift, rotation, or controlled adjustment to a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Jacks are used in bridge bearing replacement, prestressing, alignment correction, heavy lifting, erection, and temporary works.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can model jacking as an imposed displacement, applied force, or staged-construction input.

terms.definition: The force applied by a jack during lifting, adjustment, prestressing, or structural correction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Incorrect jacking force can overload bearings, piers, girders, trusses, or temporary supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow jacking force as a temporary load case.

terms.definition: A structural location where two or more members, supports, bearings, panels, cables, or mechanical components meet.
terms.engineering_relevance: Joint behaviour controls force transfer, rotation compatibility, movement release, stiffness, and stability.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat each joint as a node with assigned degrees of freedom, releases, constraints, and connection properties.

terms.definition: A local coordinate system attached to a joint or connection.
terms.engineering_relevance: Joint coordinate systems are useful for inclined supports, guided bearings, sliding joints, hinge axes, and 3D articulation.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow local joint axes for advanced joint definitions.

terms.definition: The offset between the ideal analytical joint location and the actual line of action of connected members or fasteners.
terms.engineering_relevance: Joint eccentricity causes secondary moments, torsion, local plate bending, and uneven force distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag large eccentricities and include optional secondary moment calculations.

terms.definition: A release of one or more force or moment components at a joint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Joint releases are used to model pins, hinges, sliders, torsional releases, axial releases, and mechanical articulation.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow release selection by degree of freedom and force component.

terms.definition: Relative movement at a connection due to bolt clearance, friction loss, bearing deformation, pin-hole clearance, or connection damage.
terms.engineering_relevance: Joint slip can alter stiffness, deflection, vibration, fatigue behaviour, and force distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include joint slip as a serviceability and inspection warning.

terms.definition: The resistance of a joint to relative translation or rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Real joints are rarely perfectly pinned or perfectly fixed; many behave semi-rigidly.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow translational and rotational joint stiffness values.

terms.definition: The effective length factor used to convert actual member length into effective buckling length.
terms.engineering_relevance: The value of K depends on end restraint, sway condition, rotational fixity, and joint stiffness. Articulated ends usually increase effective length compared with fixed ends.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should estimate K from end conditions and allow manual override for engineering judgement.

terms.definition: A truss arrangement where diagonal members form K-shaped patterns between verticals and chords.
terms.engineering_relevance: K-trusses distribute shear through multiple diagonal load paths and may reduce compression length in web members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include K-truss as a predefined truss geometry template.

terms.definition: A sequence of links connected by joints that permits controlled movement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Kinematic chains occur in cranes, robotic arms, scissor lifts, folding roofs, deployable shelters, movable bridges, and mechanical linkages.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify kinematic chains separately from ordinary load-bearing frames until they are locked, braced, or restrained.

terms.definition: A condition that restricts or relates the motion of one or more degrees of freedom.
terms.engineering_relevance: Examples include hinge axes, sliders, guide rails, rigid links, pin constraints, and multi-point constraints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use kinematic constraints to define deployable systems, guided joints, and mechanism behaviour.

terms.definition: The condition where the independent movement variables of a system are sufficient and non-redundant for describing its motion.
terms.engineering_relevance: A kinematically determinate system has a clear motion path without contradictory constraints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should detect whether a mechanism has a valid movement path or is blocked by over-constraint.

terms.definition: The number of independent displacement and rotation variables required to describe a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Kinematic indeterminacy is central to stiffness-method analysis because displacements are solved first.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute active degrees of freedom before assembling the global stiffness matrix.

terms.definition: The ability of a jointed system to avoid uncontrolled motion after all releases, hinges, supports, and constraints are applied.
terms.engineering_relevance: A structure may be strong member-wise but unstable as a system if the joint arrangement permits mechanism motion.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should run a kinematic stability check before reporting final structural results.

terms.definition: A system designed primarily around movement rather than only load resistance.
terms.engineering_relevance: Deployable roofs, folding frames, robotic arms, cranes, movable bridges, and scissor mechanisms are kinematic systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow a kinematic system to be analysed in both motion mode and locked structural mode.

terms.definition: The study of motion without directly considering the forces causing that motion.
terms.engineering_relevance: In articulated structures, kinematics explains how links rotate, slide, fold, expand, or lock into position.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use kinematic logic for deployable geometry, movement envelopes, hinge paths, and collision checks.

terms.definition: A short diagonal brace placed near the junction of a beam and column or rafter and column.
terms.engineering_relevance: Knee braces reduce effective span, improve lateral stability, and change local moment distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model knee braces as axial or frame members depending on connection detailing.

terms.definition: The joint where a column meets a rafter or beam, commonly seen in portal frames.
terms.engineering_relevance: The knee joint often controls frame stiffness, moment transfer, sway resistance, and connection demand.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow knee joints to be rigid, pinned, semi-rigid, or moment-released.

terms.definition: A support idealization where contact occurs along a narrow line, allowing rotation with negligible moment transfer.
terms.engineering_relevance: Knife-edge supports are common in laboratory models, theoretical mechanics, and simplified hinge support assumptions.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include knife-edge support as a hinge-like support idealization.

terms.definition: A connection point in a cable, net, membrane, lattice, or spatial articulated system.
terms.engineering_relevance: In structural geometry, a knot may behave like a node where several tension or compression paths meet.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat knots as nodes with force balance requirements and optional rotational freedom.

terms.definition: A built-up member composed of two or more main components connected by diagonal lacing bars.
terms.engineering_relevance: Laced members are used in towers, bridges, trusses, and compression members where a single solid section may be inefficient.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify laced members as built-up compression or tension members with additional local stability checks.

terms.definition: A system of diagonal connecting bars used to tie together parts of a built-up member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Lacing improves composite action and controls relative movement between member components.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include lacing as a detailing note in advanced member definition.

terms.definition: A system that restrains sideways displacement or twisting of a main member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Lateral bracing is essential for beams, rafters, arches, towers, crane booms, compression chords, and frame systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag missing lateral bracing where lateral-torsional buckling or sway instability may occur.

terms.definition: A load acting horizontally or transverse to the primary gravity direction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Wind, earthquake, braking, crane surge, soil pressure, water pressure, and impact are common lateral loads.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support lateral load cases and combine them with gravity and imposed displacement cases.

terms.definition: A restraint that prevents sideways movement of a member, joint, support, or system.
terms.engineering_relevance: Lateral restraint improves stability and reduces buckling risk.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow users to assign lateral restraint at nodes, member points, supports, and bracing locations.

terms.definition: Sideways movement of a frame, column line, tower, support, or articulated system.
terms.engineering_relevance: Sway is important in portal frames, crane frames, tall structures, bridge piers, seismic systems, and lightly braced mechanisms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify a structure as sway or non-sway where relevant.

terms.definition: Instability of a bending member involving lateral displacement and twisting.
terms.engineering_relevance: It commonly affects long unbraced beams, crane girders, rafters, bridge girders, and slender flexural members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when a bending member has large unbraced length and insufficient lateral restraint.

terms.definition: A temporary or semi-temporary structural system used to erect bridge segments, precast girders, or long-span components.
terms.engineering_relevance: Launching girders contain articulated supports, moving bearings, temporary reactions, and staged load paths.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include launching-girder logic under staged construction and temporary works.

terms.definition: The perpendicular distance between a force line of action and a reference point or axis.
terms.engineering_relevance: Lever arm controls moment magnitude and is important in pins, brackets, cranes, eccentric supports, and overturning checks.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should calculate moment as force multiplied by lever arm where relevant.

terms.definition: Loss of contact between a support and the supported structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Lift-off may occur in rocking systems, uplift-sensitive bearings, base plates, bridge decks, and compression-only supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should detect lift-off when support reaction becomes tensile in a compression-only support.

terms.definition: A condition beyond which a structure no longer satisfies a design requirement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Limit states include strength failure, instability, excessive deflection, excessive vibration, fatigue, serviceability failure, and collapse.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should separate serviceability warnings from ultimate safety warnings.

terms.definition: Analysis assuming material stress is proportional to strain and geometry changes are small.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is the usual first analysis stage for beams, frames, trusses, and articulated structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use linear elastic analysis as the default mode before advanced nonlinear options.

terms.definition: A spring where force is proportional to displacement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Linear springs represent elastic supports, soil stiffness, bearing stiffness, joint slip stiffness, and flexible restraints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use R = k∆for translational spring elements.

terms.definition: A member connecting two joints, often transmitting axial force, motion, or constraint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Links appear in trusses, cranes, scissor mechanisms, foldable frames, robotic arms, and deployable systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify links as axial-only, beam-like, rigid, flexible, or mechanism links.

terms.definition: An assembly of links connected by joints to transmit motion, force, or displacement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Linkages may be mechanical, structural, deployable, or hybrid.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include linkage templates for motion simulation and locked structural analysis.

terms.definition: Variable load caused by occupancy, people, vehicles, equipment, storage, traffic, construction activity, or movable objects.
terms.engineering_relevance: Live load changes in position or magnitude and may govern serviceability or strength.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow live-load cases and future code-based load combinations.

terms.definition: A defined scenario of applied loading, support movement, temperature change, or construction stage.
terms.engineering_relevance: Different load cases may produce different critical reactions, moments, deflections, and stability conditions.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should manage multiple load cases and compare critical outputs.

terms.definition: A rule-based combination of multiple load cases for design or assessment.
terms.engineering_relevance: Load combinations are used to evaluate safety, serviceability, and extreme event behaviour.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should initially allow custom combinations and later support code-based combinations.

terms.definition: The route by which force travels through members, joints, bearings, supports, and foundations.
terms.engineering_relevance: In articulated structures, the load path may shift from bending action to axial action or from fixed restraint to controlled movement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should generate a plain-language load-path explanation after solving.

terms.definition: The coordinate direction attached to a member, joint, bearing, or support.
terms.engineering_relevance: Local axes are used to define releases, member forces, guide directions, hinge axes, and support stiffness.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow local-axis orientation and transform results into global axes.

terms.definition: Buckling of a plate, flange, web, shell segment, gusset, or other local component.
terms.engineering_relevance: Thin-walled members and built-up steel components may fail locally before the whole member buckles.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include local-buckling notes for slender sections and gusset details.

terms.definition: A coordinate system attached to an individual member or connection rather than the whole structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: It simplifies member stiffness, end releases, hinge-axis definition, and force output.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute internally in local axes and report both local and global results.

terms.definition: The final restrained configuration of a deployable or movable structure after deployment.
terms.engineering_relevance: A mechanism may become a stable structure only after locking, bracing, or support engagement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should require locked/unlocked state definition for deployable structures.

terms.definition: A component that prevents further movement after a deployable or movable structure reaches its intended position.
terms.engineering_relevance: Locking devices convert a moving mechanism into a stable load-bearing system.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include locking devices as constraints activated in the final structural analysis stage.

terms.definition: A primary load-carrying member in a structural system.
terms.engineering_relevance: Main members include beams, columns, chords, arch ribs, crane booms, bridge girders, and major truss elements.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish main members from secondary bracing and connection elements.

terms.definition: A displacement-based structural analysis method where element stiffness matrices are assembled into a global stiffness matrix.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is the computational basis of many structural analysis programs.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use matrix stiffness logic for beams, frames, trusses, springs, semi-rigid joints, and released members.

terms.definition: A system or part of a system that can move because it has insufficient restraints or intentional kinematic freedom.
terms.engineering_relevance: Mechanisms are useful in deployable structures but dangerous in load-bearing structures unless stabilized or locked.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish accidental mechanisms from intentional deployable mechanisms.

terms.definition: A structural component connecting two or more nodes or joints.
terms.engineering_relevance: Members may act as beams, columns, bars, links, ties, struts, cables, braces, tendons, hangers, or arch ribs.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should assign every member a type, section, material, stiffness, connectivity, and release condition.

terms.definition: The reference line along the length of a structural member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Forces, eccentricities, releases, and deformations are often measured relative to the member axis.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should draw member axes clearly and allow offset or eccentric connections.

terms.definition: The force or moment component acting at the end of a member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Member end forces include axial force, shear force, bending moment, and torsion depending on model dimension.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report member end forces in both local and global coordinate systems.

terms.definition: A release applied at a member end to prevent transfer of a selected force or moment component.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moment releases are common for pin-ended members; axial and shear releases require careful use.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when end releases produce instability or disconnected force paths.

terms.definition: The internal force result within a structural member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Member force may include axial force, shear force, bending moment, and torsion.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should output member forces as diagrams, tables, and sign-classified results.

terms.definition: Load resistance through in-plane tension or compression rather than bending.
terms.engineering_relevance: Membrane action occurs in fabric structures, shells, slabs, plates, roofs, and tensioned systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include membrane action as a future extension beyond beam-frame-truss modelling.

terms.definition: An internal hinge placed near the middle of a span.
terms.engineering_relevance: Midspan hinges may be used in Gerber beams, suspended spans, and determinate beam systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow users to place internal hinges at arbitrary member locations.

terms.definition: The natural vibration pattern of a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulated structures may have low-frequency modes if joints are flexible or restraints are weak.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include modal behaviour in a future dynamic analysis module.

terms.definition: The rotational effect of a force about a point or axis.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moments create bending, overturning, twisting, and rotational demand at supports and joints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute support moments, member end moments, bending moment diagrams, and released moments.

terms.definition: A connection designed to transfer bending moment between connected members.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moment connections create continuity and stiffness but may attract thermal, settlement, and compatibility forces.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify moment connections as fixed, semi-rigid, or nonlinear moment-rotation connections.

terms.definition: The spread of bending moment through a structure according to loading, stiffness, continuity, and releases.
terms.engineering_relevance: Hinges interrupt moment continuity; semi-rigid joints partially redistribute moment.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should visualize how moment changes when a user changes joint type.

terms.definition: A frame system in which lateral resistance is provided mainly by moment-resisting joints.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moment frames depend on beam-column joint stiffness and ductility.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify moment frames separately from braced frames and pin-jointed trusses.

terms.definition: A modelling condition where bending moment transfer is removed at a member end, joint, or internal point.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moment releases represent pins, hinges, bearing rotations, or flexible connections.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should show zero bending moment at ideal moment releases and rerun stability checks after every release change.

terms.definition: The relationship between bending moment and joint rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: A perfectly pinned joint has nearly zero moment resistance, a fixed joint has very high rotational stiffness, and a semi-rigid joint lies between them.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support linear M = kθθ first and later nonlinear moment-rotation curves.

terms.definition: A load whose position changes along a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Moving loads are important for bridges, cranes, rails, gantries, vehicles, conveyors, and construction equipment.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include moving-load envelopes and influence-line support in advanced mode.

terms.definition: A constraint equation linking displacement or rotation values at multiple nodes.
terms.engineering_relevance: Multi-point constraints are used for rigid links, diaphragm action, tied nodes, guided motion, symmetry, and mechanism relationships.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use multi-point constraints for advanced articulated and kinematic models.

terms.definition: A beam continuous over more than one span.
terms.engineering_relevance: Multi-span beams may be continuous, articulated, Gerber-type, bearing-supported, or settlement-sensitive.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support internal supports, hinges, releases, and span-wise diagrams.

terms.definition: A geometry that can change configuration during deployment, loading, actuation, or staged construction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Mutable geometry is central to deployable structures, moving bridges, cranes, scissor systems, and adaptive structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat mutable geometry as a separate modelling mode from fixed structural geometry.

terms.definition: The frequency at which a structure tends to vibrate freely after being disturbed.
terms.engineering_relevance: Articulated systems with flexible joints, cables, bearings, or light members may have low natural frequencies and vibration sensitivity.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include natural frequency as a future dynamic-analysis output.

terms.definition: A structural model whose stiffness matrix is almost singular because restraints are weak, releases are excessive, or geometry is close to mechanism behaviour.
terms.engineering_relevance: Near-singular systems may produce very large displacements or unreliable numerical results.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn users when the stiffness matrix has poor conditioning.

terms.definition: The axis in a bending member where normal stress is zero under pure bending.
terms.engineering_relevance: Neutral-axis position affects bending stress, curvature, cracking, and composite action.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can use neutral-axis logic in future section-stress and design-check modules.

terms.definition: The translation or rotation calculated at a node.
terms.engineering_relevance: Nodal displacements are primary unknowns in matrix stiffness analysis.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should output nodal displacement tables and deformed-shape plots.

terms.definition: A load applied directly at a node rather than along a member.
terms.engineering_relevance: Nodal loads are useful for joint loads, point masses, actuator forces, cable forces, and idealized external actions.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow nodal force and nodal moment input.

terms.definition: A modelling point where members, supports, loads, springs, constraints, or joints are connected.
terms.engineering_relevance: Nodes are the computational equivalent of joints in structural analysis.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should assign coordinates, degrees of freedom, restraints, loads, and joint properties to every node.

terms.definition: A frame whose lateral translation is restrained by bracing, walls, supports, or other stabilizing systems.
terms.engineering_relevance: Non-sway behaviour reduces second-order effects and changes column effective length.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify frames as sway or non-sway for stability notes.

terms.definition: Analysis where the relationship between load and response is not proportional.
terms.engineering_relevance: Nonlinearity may arise from large displacement, material yielding, contact, uplift, cable sag, friction, or joint slip.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should separate linear default analysis from advanced nonlinear analysis modes.

terms.definition: The ability of a computational solution to remain reliable and well-conditioned.
terms.engineering_relevance: Bad scaling, weak springs, excessive releases, duplicate constraints, and mechanism modes can reduce numerical stability.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should provide solver health warnings rather than only error messages.

terms.definition: A connection where the physical member line does not pass exactly through the ideal analytical joint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Offsets create eccentricity, secondary bending, torsion, and local connection demand.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow connection offsets and warn when the idealized model ignores significant eccentricity.

terms.definition: Elongation or distortion of a circular hole, tube, shell, or pin connection under repeated or high bearing stress.
terms.engineering_relevance: Ovalized pin holes can increase joint slip, reduce stiffness, and accelerate fatigue damage.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include ovalization as an inspection defect term for pin-connected structures.

terms.definition: A system with more restraints than necessary, possibly causing locked-in forces from temperature, settlement, shrinkage, or construction tolerance.
terms.engineering_relevance: Over-constraint is not always unsafe, but it can create unintended internal forces.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag duplicate or conflicting restraints.

terms.definition: A modelling condition where too many force or moment components are released.
terms.engineering_relevance: Over-release can convert a stable structure into a mechanism.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should automatically run stability checks after every release assignment.

terms.definition: A moment that tends to rotate or topple a structure, support, foundation, crane, frame, or wall.
terms.engineering_relevance: Overturning is important in cranes, retaining systems, towers, portal frames, bridge piers, and base-isolated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include overturning checks for support reactions and lateral load cases.

terms.definition: A joint location in a truss or framed system where members meet and loads are ideally applied.
terms.engineering_relevance: Applying loads at panel points helps maintain axial-force behaviour in ideal truss members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should identify panel points and warn when loads are applied between them in axial-only truss models.

terms.definition: A condition where a connection transfers some moment but is not perfectly rigid.
terms.engineering_relevance: Partial fixity is common in real bolted, welded, bearing, timber, and precast connections.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model partial fixity using rotational stiffness or moment-rotation curves.

terms.definition: A release condition between fully fixed and fully free.
terms.engineering_relevance: A partially released joint has finite stiffness and transfers limited force or moment.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support partial releases through spring stiffness values.

terms.definition: The local compressive contact stress between a pin and the plate or lug hole around it.
terms.engineering_relevance: Pin bearing controls local crushing, ovalization, wear, and fatigue in articulated joints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include pin-bearing checks in a connection-design extension.

terms.definition: A physical connection where a pin passes through aligned holes to permit rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Pin connections appear in trusses, cranes, tie rods, clevises, linkages, and bridge components.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify pin connections as articulated joints and include pin force output.

terms.definition: A joint that transfers force while allowing rotation and ideally transferring no bending moment.
terms.engineering_relevance: Pinned joints are used in trusses, cranes, linkages, arches, brackets, temporary works, and articulated frames.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model pinned joints as rotational releases with selected force transfer preserved.

terms.definition: A support that restrains translation but allows rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: In a 2D model, a pinned support usually provides horizontal and vertical reactions but no moment reaction.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should assign translational restraints and release rotational restraint for pinned supports.

terms.definition: A localized region where a member reaches plastic moment capacity and rotates with limited increase in moment.
terms.engineering_relevance: Plastic hinges are important in collapse mechanisms, seismic design, ductility, and ultimate limit analysis.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include plastic hinge logic in an advanced nonlinear or collapse-mode module.

terms.definition: A frame with columns and rafters or beams, commonly used in industrial buildings, sheds, warehouses, and halls.
terms.engineering_relevance: Portal frames may have pinned bases, fixed bases, rigid knees, semi-rigid joints, or ridge hinges.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include portal-frame templates with selectable base and knee joint conditions.

terms.definition: A bridge bearing where elastomer is confined within a steel pot, allowing high vertical load and controlled rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Pot bearings are used where heavy loads and rotational capacity are required.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify pot bearings under bridge-bearing support types.

terms.definition: A deliberate internal force introduced before service loading, usually through tendons, jacks, or tensioning devices.
terms.engineering_relevance: Prestress can control deflection, cracking, uplift, cable sag, and structural stiffness.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow prestress as an initial load or member force input.

terms.definition: A main load-carrying component of a structure.
terms.engineering_relevance: Primary members form the essential load path from applied loads to supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish primary members from secondary bracing, cladding supports, and detailing elements.

terms.definition: Additional force in bolts, pins, or fasteners caused by deformation of connected plates.
terms.engineering_relevance: Prying action can significantly increase fastener tension beyond direct load estimates.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include prying action as a connection warning in detailed design mode.

terms.definition: A four-link mechanism that can change shape unless braced, triangulated, or otherwise restrained.
terms.engineering_relevance: Unbraced rectangular frames may behave like quadrilateral mechanisms when joints are pinned.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when a quadrilateral bay lacks diagonal bracing or moment-resisting joints.

terms.definition: A load applied slowly enough that inertial effects are small.
terms.engineering_relevance: Many structural loads are treated as quasi-static even if they vary gradually over time.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use quasi-static assumptions in default linear analysis while warning for impact or vibration-sensitive cases.

terms.definition: A force or moment developed at a support, bearing, spring, or restraint in response to applied loads and imposed movements.
terms.engineering_relevance: Reaction components depend on the support type and released degrees of freedom.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report reactions according to each support’s actual restraints.

terms.definition: Extra restraint or alternative load path beyond the minimum required for stability.
terms.engineering_relevance: Redundancy improves robustness but also introduces compatibility forces and indeterminacy.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should identify redundant restraints and explain their effect on analysis method.

terms.definition: A modelling condition that removes or reduces transfer of a selected force or moment component.
terms.engineering_relevance: Releases are used to represent hinges, pins, sliders, torsional freedoms, axial freedoms, and semi-rigid behaviour.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should make releases visible in diagrams and rerun stability checks after release changes.

terms.definition: Unbalanced force remaining after a numerical solution or equilibrium check.
terms.engineering_relevance: Large residual forces may indicate convergence problems, modelling errors, or unstable nonlinear behaviour.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report residuals as solver health indicators.

terms.definition: A support, connection, spring, bearing, guide, brace, or constraint that limits movement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Restraints control stability, reactions, deflections, and internal force distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify restraints by direction, stiffness, and force component.
