terms.definition: Movement of an entire structure or part of a structure without deformation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rigid body motion usually indicates inadequate restraint unless it is intentionally allowed in a mechanism.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should detect rigid body modes and explain which restraint is missing.

terms.definition: A joint that enforces common movement and rotation among connected members.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rigid joints transfer moment and maintain angle compatibility between members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model rigid joints using full displacement and rotation compatibility.

terms.definition: A modelling element that transfers motion between nodes while assuming negligible deformation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rigid links are useful for offsets, eccentric joints, diaphragm constraints, and connection arms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include rigid links as non-deforming constraint elements.

terms.definition: A bearing that allows rotation through rocking action while transferring vertical load.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rocker bearings were historically used in bridges and may be sensitive to corrosion, instability, and misalignment.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify rocker bearings as rotation-permitting support devices.

terms.definition: A structural system that allows controlled uplift and rotation at its base or contact surface.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rocking systems can reduce seismic damage if restoring force and displacement capacity are properly controlled.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model rocking through compression-only contact, uplift detection, and restoring force logic.

terms.definition: A support that restrains movement normal to its surface while allowing movement parallel to the surface and rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Roller supports are used in beam idealizations, bridge bearings, expansion supports, and guided movement systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should define roller direction clearly to avoid incorrect reaction orientation.

terms.definition: Angular movement of a member, joint, support, or body.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rotation is central to hinges, bearings, semi-rigid joints, rocking systems, and plastic hinges.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should output rotations in radians and optionally degrees.

terms.definition: An independent angular movement variable at a node or joint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rotational degrees of freedom determine whether moments can be transferred or released.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should track active, restrained, released, and spring-supported rotational DOFs.

terms.definition: A spring that resists rotation with a moment proportional to angular displacement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Rotational springs represent semi-rigid joints, flexible bases, bearing rotation stiffness, and partial fixity.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use M = kθθ for linear rotational spring behaviour.

terms.definition: A deployable mechanism formed by crossing links connected by pins, allowing expansion and contraction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Scissor systems are used in lifts, temporary roofs, deployable shelters, kinetic facades, and adjustable platforms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model scissor mechanisms in kinematic mode and locked structural mode.

terms.definition: An additional force or moment caused by structural deformation under load.
terms.engineering_relevance: Examples include P∆ effects in frames and Pδ effects in compression members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag second-order sensitivity in slender, sway, or compression-dominant systems.

terms.definition: A member that supports or stabilizes primary members but is not part of the main load path.
terms.engineering_relevance: Secondary members include purlins, bracing, lacing, hangers, cross-members, and minor support elements.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish secondary members from primary members in reports and diagrams.

terms.definition: A moment generated by eccentricity, deformation, compatibility, support movement, or second-order effects rather than direct applied bending.
terms.engineering_relevance: Secondary moments can be important in articulated systems where ideal pin assumptions hide real eccentricity.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when eccentric joints or support movements may generate secondary moments.

terms.definition: A joint that transfers partial moment and allows finite rotation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Semi-rigid joints are more realistic than ideal pinned or ideal fixed assumptions for many bolted, welded, timber, precast, and bearing-based connections.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model semi-rigid joints using rotational stiffness or moment-rotation curves.

terms.definition: The performance of a structure under normal use conditions.
terms.engineering_relevance: Serviceability includes deflection, vibration, cracking, drift, movement, rotation, comfort, appearance, and operational limits.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should separate serviceability warnings from ultimate strength warnings.

terms.definition: Vertical or horizontal movement of a support or foundation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Settlement can create compatibility forces in indeterminate structures and rotation in articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow support settlement as an imposed displacement load case.

terms.definition: Internal transverse force acting across a member section.
terms.engineering_relevance: Shear force is important in beams, frames, pins, gusset plates, bearings, short members, and support regions.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should output shear force diagrams and shear reaction tables.

terms.definition: A structural feature used to transfer or resist lateral shear movement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Shear keys are used in bridge bearings, foundations, retaining structures, precast joints, and seismic detailing.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify shear keys as lateral restraint components.

terms.definition: A release that prevents transfer of shear force in a selected direction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Shear releases are less common than moment releases and must be used carefully because they may create instability.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when shear releases break the load path.

terms.definition: A stiffness matrix that cannot be inverted because the system is unstable, under-constrained, or has dependent constraints.
terms.engineering_relevance: This often occurs when hinges, rollers, or releases are added CHAPTER 2. ARTICULATED STRUCTURES: CORE FRAMEWORK without enough stabilizing restraint.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should translate singular matrix errors into understandable engineering warnings. 2.8 Compatibility and Stiffness

terms.definition: A measure of how long and thin a compression member is relative to its buckling resistance.
terms.engineering_relevance: High slenderness increases buckling risk in struts, columns, braces, arch ribs, and compression chords.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag slender compression members for buckling checks.

terms.definition: A joint that permits translation along a specified path while restraining other movements.
terms.engineering_relevance: Slider joints occur in guide rails, movable supports, mechanical linkages, and deployable systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should define slider joints using a local guide axis.

terms.definition: A bearing that permits translation along a low-friction surface while transferring vertical load.
terms.engineering_relevance: Sliding bearings accommodate thermal expansion, creep, shrinkage, and long-span movement.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should define sliding direction, friction condition, and movement capacity.

terms.definition: A sudden jump from one equilibrium configuration to another.
terms.engineering_relevance: Snap-through can occur in shallow arches, shells, deployable structures, bistable systems, and geometrically nonlinear frames.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should mark snap-through as an advanced nonlinear stability phenomenon.

terms.definition: A bearing with curved sliding surfaces that permits rotation about multiple axes.
terms.engineering_relevance: Spherical bearings are used where large multi-axis rotations and high load capacity are required.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include spherical bearing as a 3D rotation-capable support.

terms.definition: A joint that allows rotation about multiple axes while restraining selected translations.
terms.engineering_relevance: Spherical joints are common in spatial linkages, robotic systems, mechanical supports, and some articulated structural assemblies.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model spherical joints with released rotational degrees of freedom and restrained translational degrees of freedom.

terms.definition: A support that resists displacement or rotation through finite stiffness.
terms.engineering_relevance: Spring supports represent soil flexibility, bearing pads, elastomeric supports, flexible bases, and partial restraints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow translational and rotational spring support input.

terms.definition: The ability of a structure to avoid uncontrolled displacement, rotation, collapse, or mechanism formation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Stability depends on geometry, support arrangement, joint restraints, member stiffness, and load path.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should run stability checks before presenting force and deflection results.

terms.definition: A condition where all unknown reactions and internal forces can be solved using equilibrium equations alone.
terms.engineering_relevance: Determinate structures are easier to analyse but may have less redundancy.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify determinate systems separately from indeterminate and unstable systems.

terms.definition: A condition where unknown reactions or internal forces exceed available independent equilibrium equations.
terms.engineering_relevance: Indeterminate structures require compatibility, stiffness, or force-method analysis.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should use indeterminacy classification to select the appropriate solver.

terms.definition: Resistance to displacement or rotation under applied force or moment.
terms.engineering_relevance: Stiffness may be axial EA/L, flexural EI, torsional GJ/L, translational spring stiffness k, or rotational stiffness kθ.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow users to define member stiffness, support stiffness, and joint stiffness. Formula / Relation Axial deformation of a prismatic member: ∆= NL EA where N is axial force, L is member length, E is Young’s modulus, and A is cross-sectional area. Formula / Relation Linear spring reaction: R = k∆ where R is reaction, k is translational stiffness, and ∆is displacement. Formula / Relation Semi-rigid rotational joint: M = kθθ where M is moment, kθ is rotational stiffness, and θ is relative rotation.

terms.definition: A matrix that relates nodal forces to nodal displacements in structural analysis.
terms.engineering_relevance: The stiffness matrix is central to computational analysis of beams, frames, trusses, springs, and semi-rigid joints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should assemble the global stiffness matrix internally and translate errors into readable warnings.

terms.definition: A member primarily carrying compression.
terms.engineering_relevance: Struts are common in trusses, braces, cranes, towers, linkages, and temporary works.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify struts as compression members and check buckling sensitivity.

terms.definition: The force or moment generated at a support due to applied loads, imposed movements, and constraints.
terms.engineering_relevance: Support reactions depend on support type, structure geometry, stiffness, and load case.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report reactions with correct direction and units.

terms.definition: A frame that can translate laterally under load because it lacks sufficient lateral restraint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Sway frames are more sensitive to second-order effects and stability problems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify frames as sway or non-sway where relevant.

terms.definition: The instantaneous stiffness of a nonlinear system at a particular load or displacement state.
terms.engineering_relevance: Tangent stiffness is important when joint stiffness, cable geometry, contact, material yielding, or large displacement changes during loading.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can use tangent stiffness in future nonlinear analysis modules.

terms.definition: Temporary structural systems used during construction, lifting, launching, repair, inspection, or staging.
terms.engineering_relevance: Temporary works often contain articulated supports, jacks, props, pins, rollers, scaffolds, launching systems, and staged load paths.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include temporary works as a special modelling category with construction-stage warnings.

terms.definition: A tension element used to apply prestress, restore force, or hold structural components together.
terms.engineering_relevance: Tendons are used in prestressed concrete, tied arches, rocking systems, cable-supported systems, and post-tensioned members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow tendon force as prestress, initial strain, or controlled tension input.

terms.definition: A member primarily carrying axial tension.
terms.engineering_relevance: Tension members include ties, hangers, rods, cables, tendons, and some truss members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify tension members separately from compression members and display tension force clearly.

alternate_entries.definition: A member primarily carrying axial tension.
alternate_entries.engineering_relevance: Tension members include ties, hangers, rods, cables, tendons, and some truss members.
alternate_entries.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify tension members separately from compression members.

terms.definition: A member that can resist tensile force but cannot resist compression.
terms.engineering_relevance: Cables, hangers, flexible rods, and slack-prone ties are commonly treated as tension-only members.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should deactivate or flag the member when calculated force becomes compressive.

alternate_entries.definition: A member that can resist tension but cannot resist compression.
alternate_entries.engineering_relevance: Cables, flexible rods, hangers, and slack-prone ties may behave as tension-only members.
alternate_entries.app_solver_relevance: The app should remove or deactivate the member in compression during nonlinear or tension-only checks.

terms.definition: Decrease in length, area, or volume due to temperature reduction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Thermal contraction can open joints, increase bearing movement, change cable force, or create restraint effects.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should treat contraction as a temperature-change load case with sign-sensitive displacement.

terms.definition: Increase in length, area, or volume due to temperature rise.
terms.engineering_relevance: Thermal expansion is critical in bridges, roofs, rails, pipelines, long-span buildings, and bearing-supported structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow temperature load cases and compute free or restrained thermal movement.

alternate_entries.definition: Increase in length or size due to temperature rise.
alternate_entries.engineering_relevance: Thermal expansion is important in bridges, roofs, long buildings, pipelines, rails, and bearing-supported structures.
alternate_entries.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow temperature load cases and expansion-joint movement checks.

terms.definition: Development of unwanted internal force because a structure is prevented from expanding or contracting freely.
terms.engineering_relevance: Thermal lock-in may occur when expansion bearings seize, joints close, or supports are over-constrained.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when temperature movement is blocked by fixed, guided, or seized restraints.

alternate_entries.definition: Development of unwanted internal force because thermal movement is restrained.
alternate_entries.engineering_relevance: Thermal lock-in can occur when expansion bearings seize or when long structures are over-constrained.
alternate_entries.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when thermal movement is restrained by fixed or seized supports.

terms.definition: Movement caused by expansion or contraction due to temperature change.
terms.engineering_relevance: It must be accommodated through bearings, expansion joints, sliding supports, flexible details, or release zones.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compare calculated thermal movement with bearing or expansion-joint capacity.

terms.definition: An arch with two support hinges and one internal crown hinge.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is generally statically determinate and tolerant of support settlement and temperature effects.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include a three-hinged arch template with thrust, hinge force, reaction, and bending outputs.

alternate_entries.definition: An arch with hinges at both supports and one internal crown hinge.
alternate_entries.engineering_relevance: It is usually statically determinate and tolerant of settlement and temperature movement.
alternate_entries.app_solver_relevance: The app should include a three-hinged arch template with crown hinge force and thrust outputs.

terms.definition: A frame with two support hinges and one internal hinge, usually at the ridge, crown, or selected frame location.
terms.engineering_relevance: Three-hinged frames reduce restraint moments and are often easier to analyse using equilibrium.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include three-hinged frame templates for portals, roofs, and articulated frame systems.

alternate_entries.definition: A frame with two support hinges and one internal hinge, commonly at the ridge or crown.
alternate_entries.engineering_relevance: Three-hinged frames are commonly determinate and reduce moment demand from support settlement.
alternate_entries.app_solver_relevance: The app should include three-hinged frame templates for portal and roof systems.

terms.definition: A tension member used to restrain separation, resist thrust, or connect two structural parts.
terms.engineering_relevance: Ties are used in tied arches, roof trusses, bracing systems, temporary works, and tensioned assemblies.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify ties as tension-dominant members and report tie force.

alternate_entries.definition: A member used to carry tension and restrain separation or thrust.
alternate_entries.engineering_relevance: Ties are used in tied arches, roof trusses, bracing systems

terms.definition: An arch in which horizontal thrust is resisted by a tie member rather than entirely by foundations.
terms.engineering_relevance: Tied arches reduce foundation thrust demand and transfer major force into the tie.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should compute arch compression, tie tension, hanger force, deck force, and support reactions.

terms.definition: A linkage mechanism that passes through or approaches a near-straight configuration, often producing high mechanical advantage.
terms.engineering_relevance: Toggle effects can create very large internal forces near the locked position.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should warn when a linkage approaches a near-toggle or force-amplifying configuration.

terms.definition: Permitted variation in geometry, alignment, level, hole position, member length, or installation position.
terms.engineering_relevance: Tolerance matters in pin joints, bearings, segmental bridges, steel frames, precast systems, and deployable structures.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include tolerance as a reality-check parameter in inspection and constructability mode.

terms.definition: Twisting moment about a member’s longitudinal axis.
terms.engineering_relevance: Torsion occurs in curved members, eccentric connections, bridge decks, off-axis loads, space frames, and 3D articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should support torsional stiffness, torsional release, and torsion result output in 3D mode.

terms.definition: A release that prevents torsional moment transfer about a selected axis.
terms.engineering_relevance: Torsional releases are useful in 3D modelling of bearings, shafts, links, spatial joints, and mechanical articulations.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should show released torsional degrees of freedom explicitly.

terms.definition: An independent linear movement variable at a node, support, joint, or body.
terms.engineering_relevance: Translation may occur horizontally, vertically, longitudinally, transversely, or along a guide direction.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should track free, restrained, spring-supported, imposed, gap-controlled, and compression-only translations.

terms.definition: A spring that resists linear displacement with force proportional to displacement.
terms.engineering_relevance: Translational springs represent soil stiffness, bearing stiffness, elastic supports, guide flexibility, and flexible restraints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should model linear translational spring behaviour using R = k∆.

terms.definition: A structural system made of members connected at joints, ideally carrying axial tension or compression.
terms.engineering_relevance: Ideal truss analysis assumes loads are applied at joints and members do not transfer bending moment.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include truss templates and warn when bending effects invalidate ideal truss assumptions.

terms.definition: The bay or segment between adjacent truss panel points.
terms.engineering_relevance: Panel geometry controls web member force, buckling length, deflection, and load distribution.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow panel-based truss generation and panel force reporting.

terms.definition: An arch with hinges at both supports and no crown hinge.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is usually statically indeterminate to the first degree because horizontal thrust depends on compatibility.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should solve two-hinged arches using stiffness or compatibility-based methods.

terms.definition: A frame with hinged supports but moment continuity in the main frame members.
terms.engineering_relevance: Its determinacy depends on geometry, releases, and member continuity.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify two-hinged frames by support restraints and joint continuity.

terms.definition: A safety condition associated with collapse, rupture, instability, overturning, excessive yielding, or loss of equilibrium.
terms.engineering_relevance: Ultimate limit states protect against structural failure under extreme or factored loading.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should separate ultimate warnings from serviceability warnings.

terms.definition: A force remaining after equilibrium has not been fully satisfied.
terms.engineering_relevance: Unbalanced force may indicate solver convergence problems, missing restraints, numerical instability, or incorrect load application.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report unbalanced force as a solver health warning.

terms.definition: A system with insufficient restraints to prevent rigid body motion or mechanism formation.
terms.engineering_relevance: Under-constrained systems often produce singular stiffness matrices and unrealistic displacements.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should identify likely missing restraints and suggest correction points.

terms.definition: A condition where a joint or support intended to rotate or slide freely behaves as partially or fully fixed.
terms.engineering_relevance: Unintended fixity may arise from corrosion, debris, friction, construction error, locked bearings, or rigid secondary components.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include unintended fixity as a reality-check and inspection warning.

terms.definition: A condition where a joint intended to transfer force or moment loses stiffness, continuity, or restraint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Unintended release may occur due to cracking, bolt slip, weld failure, pin wear, bearing damage, or deterioration.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include unintended release as a defect and diagnostic warning.

terms.definition: A joint that permits rotation between two shafts or members whose axes are not aligned.
terms.engineering_relevance: Universal joints are common in mechanical systems and may appear in movable, adaptive, or deployable structural systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can classify universal joints under multi-axis articulated joint types.

terms.definition: The length of a member between points of effective lateral, torsional, or rotational restraint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Unrestrained length controls buckling, lateral-torsional buckling, and slenderness sensitivity.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should identify unrestrained lengths for beams, struts, braces, compression chords, and rafters.

terms.definition: Loss of contact or upward movement at a support, bearing, base plate, foundation, or contact surface.
terms.engineering_relevance: Uplift occurs in rocking systems, wind-loaded roofs, seismic overturning, bridge bearings, and compression-only supports.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should detect uplift when a compression-only support reaction becomes tensile.

terms.definition: A structural configuration whose shape can change during deployment, actuation, construction, or service.
terms.engineering_relevance: Variable geometry appears in cranes, movable bridges, deployable roofs, scissor structures, folding systems, and adaptive facades.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify variable-geometry systems separately from fixed-geometry structural models.

terms.definition: A stiffness condition that changes with load, displacement, damage, temperature, contact state, or control input.
terms.engineering_relevance: Variable stiffness appears in nonlinear bearings, adaptive structures, yielding joints, soil supports, cables, and deployable systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include variable stiffness in advanced nonlinear and adaptive modules.

terms.definition: The assembled force vector applied to the active degrees of freedom of a structural model.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is used with the global stiffness matrix to solve for nodal displacements.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should build this internally from point loads, member loads, equivalent nodal loads, and imposed effects.

terms.definition: The vertical component of support force.
terms.engineering_relevance: Vertical reactions are fundamental outputs for beams, frames, arches, trusses, bearings, and foundations.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should report vertical reactions with sign convention and load-case association.

terms.definition: Repeated oscillatory motion of a structure, member, joint, cable, or support system.
terms.engineering_relevance: Flexible articulated systems, cables, bridges, cranes, roofs, and machinery supports may be vibration-sensitive.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should flag vibration-sensitive models for future dynamic analysis.

terms.definition: An energy method used to compute displacement or establish equilibrium through virtual forces or virtual displacements.
terms.engineering_relevance: Virtual work is useful for trusses, beams, frames, arches, and articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can use virtual-work explanations in educational mode.

terms.definition: A damping device whose resisting force depends on velocity.
terms.engineering_relevance: Viscous dampers are used in seismic protection, vibration control, bridge systems, tall structures, and adaptive systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include viscous dampers in future dynamic and seismic modules.

terms.definition: Progressive material loss due to repeated contact, rotation, sliding, abrasion, or vibration.
terms.engineering_relevance: Wear is important in pins, hinges, bearings, rollers, sliding plates, guide rails, and moving joints.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include wear as an inspection defect category.

terms.definition: A diagonal or vertical member connecting the top and bottom chords of a truss or girder.
terms.engineering_relevance: Web members usually carry axial force and help transfer shear through a truss system.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should classify web members as tension, compression, or zero-force members depending on load case.

terms.definition: Load caused by wind pressure, suction, drag, or dynamic wind effects.
terms.engineering_relevance: Wind load is important for roofs, towers, facades, bridges, cranes, temporary works, and lightweight articulated systems.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include wind load as lateral, uplift, suction, or pressure loading.

terms.definition: An analysis method based on the relationship between external work and internal strain energy.
terms.engineering_relevance: It is useful for displacement estimation, stability concepts, collapse mechanisms, and educational explanation.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include work-energy explanation blocks in educational mode.

terms.definition: The unfactored service load expected during normal operation or use.
terms.engineering_relevance: Working load is used for serviceability checks, deflection review, bearing movement, and operational safety.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should distinguish working load from factored or ultimate load.

terms.definition: A bracing arrangement where two diagonal members cross to form an X shape.
terms.engineering_relevance: X-bracing improves lateral stability and prevents quadrilateral frame mechanisms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should include X-bracing as a predefined bracing template.

terms.definition: A load acting along the global or local X direction.
terms.engineering_relevance: X-direction loads may represent wind, seismic force, braking force, crane surge, actuator force, or lateral thrust.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should allow directional load input in global or local coordinates.

terms.definition: A restraint that prevents movement along the global or local X direction.
terms.engineering_relevance: Directional restraints are essential in 2D and 3D support modelling.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should show X-direction restraints graphically to avoid incorrect support assumptions.

terms.definition: A line along which plastic rotation concentrates in a slab, plate, or shell.
terms.engineering_relevance: Yield-line mechanisms are important in collapse analysis of plates and slabs.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include yield-line logic as a future plate and shell extension.

terms.definition: The bending moment at which a section first reaches yield stress at its extreme fibre.
terms.engineering_relevance: Yield moment marks the transition from elastic bending to inelastic behaviour.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include yield moment in future section-capacity and plastic-hinge checks.

terms.definition: Material behaviour where deformation continues beyond the elastic range and permanent strain develops.
terms.engineering_relevance: Yielding can produce plastic hinges, energy dissipation, redistribution, and collapse mechanisms.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app can include yielding in advanced nonlinear and plasticanalysis modules.

terms.definition: A location where bending moment is zero.
terms.engineering_relevance: Hinges are ideal zero-moment points, but zero moment can also occur naturally within a span due to loading and continuity.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should mark zero-moment locations on bending moment diagrams.

terms.definition: A boundary condition where displacement in a selected direction is fixed to zero.
terms.engineering_relevance: Zero-displacement boundaries represent supports, restraints, symmetry planes, or fixed movement directions.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should assign zero-displacement conditions through support and restraint definitions.

terms.definition: A deformation mode that occurs without strain energy because the model lacks sufficient stiffness or restraint.
terms.engineering_relevance: Zero-energy modes indicate mechanisms, missing constraints, poor element formulation, or unstable release patterns.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should detect zero-energy modes and explain likely modelling causes.

terms.definition: A truss member that carries no axial force under a particular load case.
terms.engineering_relevance: Zero-force members may still be useful for stability, construction, alternate load cases, or bracing.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should identify zero-force members but avoid automatically deleting them from the model.

terms.definition: A local region where movement, rotation, sliding, or force release is intentionally concentrated.
terms.engineering_relevance: Zones of articulation include hinges, bearings, expansion joints, sliding seats, rocker supports, and mechanical linkages.
terms.app_solver_relevance: The app should mark articulation zones clearly in diagrams and reports.
